subject: music
topicName: Free Composition and Composing to a Brief

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Free composition allows you to choose your own starting point — a melody, chord progression, rhythm or concept that inspires you.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Composing to a brief requires interpreting AQA's stimulus: read carefully, identify the musical implications, plan how you will respond to each element.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Both compositions must be at least 1 minute each — the score must be in staff notation (up to 4 sharps/flats) with a recording.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: AO2 marks: technical control (accuracy of notation, appropriate writing for instruments), coherence (logical structure, development), creative development (inventive use of elements).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe how free composition and composing to a brief are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use free composition and composing to a brief. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use free composition and composing to a brief in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A detailed description using precise musical vocabulary (e.g. specific terms from the AQA elements list), referencing a named piece with accurate observations about how the elements are used and their | A comparison of two pieces identifying similarities and differences in how free composition and composing to a brief are used, explaining the different effects created in each musical context, using c | A practical application showing understanding of how free composition and composing to a brief can be manipulated in composition or performance, with specific examples of choices made and their intend

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use PRECISE musical vocabulary — not vague descriptions like it sounds nice Reference SPECIFIC musical elements when analysing any piece For listening questions: identify elements FIRST, then explain their effect For study pieces: know the context, structure and key features in detail For performing: focus on accuracy, expression and interpretation For composing: show development of ideas, not just repetition
